attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. He is not quoting anyone else.

semantics.note: 'Growing evidence' describes evidence that already exists, so this is an observation, not a hedge. 'Feed the beast' means keeping LLM scaling going, and the normalised proposition keeps that scope.

contract.note: The plain reading (evidence that usable data limits further scaling) is fair and ordinary. Reading 'we just don't have enough' as data already used up would be harsher than the context supports. The result depends on choosing the constraint reading over present exhaustion.

evidence.note: Epoch AI, June 2024: estimates a finite stock of usable human text, fully used by about 2026-2032 at current scaling. That is a finite supply that scaling would overtake. Its estimate is more generous than the 2022 version, which tempers 'growing'.
Longpre et al., July 2024: audit finds web data for training was rapidly being restricted in 2023-24. This is evidence of practical limits on usable supply, if the restrictions are respected.
April 2024 study: keeping real data alongside generated data avoids model collapse. This qualifies the synthetic-data worry but does not show the supply can sustain continued frontier scaling.

reviews.rationale: By the post date, research in the packet showed a finite usable text supply that scaling was projected to exhaust (e1) and fast-growing access restrictions (e2). That meets the support condition. e3 and Epoch's more generous estimate qualify the picture, but neither shows the supply can meet continued scaling, so the contradiction condition is not met.
